summary: The waterfront arts-building parcel east of Building 21: excluded from the developer's purchase option, capped at 50 ft and five stories, and reserved under the 2017 DDA for a roughly 90,000 sq ft arts facility (with replacement studios for the Noonan Building artists) on a 50-year, $1-a-year lease once $17.5 million in private contributions is raised. The Port's proposed 2026 amendments would rezone it to allow housing if the arts facility proves infeasible.

milestones.text: Planning Commission certifies the Pier 70 Mixed-Use Project Final EIR (Case 2014-001272ENV, Motion 19976) and approves the Design for Development (Resolution 19980)

Port Commission approves the Disposition and Development Agreement with FC Pier 70, LLC (Resolution 17-43), consents to the Pier 70 Special Use District and the D4D (17-45) and the Development Agreement (17-47)
Mayor Lee signs the Development Agreement ordinance (Ordinance 224-17) and the rest of the project legislation after Board of Supervisors approval on October 31, 2017
Disposition and Development Agreement dated as of May 2, 2018; the Port approves the Phase 1 Submittal the same month
Groundbreaking for Phase 1 (horizontal infrastructure, Building 12, parks) announced by the Port
Phase 1 site preparation and demolition begin; utility and street construction on 20th, Maryland, Louisiana, 21st and 22nd Streets follows in March 2019
Final appraisal of Parcel E2 comes in below its DDA threshold value, triggering a Phase 1 'down market delay' that tolls the developer's deadlines to close on option parcels
Brookfield halts construction at the end of Phase 1 horizontal work, citing market conditions
City issues Notice of Completion for the Phase 1 infrastructure, described by Brookfield as a $150 million investment
Phase 1 streets and utilities accepted by the City and Port; streets around Pier 70 opened to the public in May 2024
Phase 1 down market delay reaches its 60-month maximum; the parties extend it by six months to December 26, 2026 while DDA amendments are drafted

Port Commission hears an informational report on proposed DDA amendments: parcel-specific outside dates, a Project-wide affordable rate of no less than 20% (327 stand-alone affordable units kept), 65-to-90 ft height increases on certain residential parcels, developer return cut from 18% to 14%, and a new phasing plan
Amendments to the DDA, Development Agreement and Master Lease expected before the Port Commission and Board of Supervisors 'by the end of this year or early next year'

Proposed DDA amendment: change the zoning of Parcel E4 to allow residential use if an arts facility is infeasible, with Noonan Building tenants' replacement space provided in other buildings; this and 65-to-90 ft height increases 'could result in an additional 600 homes on site'

costs.what: Private charitable contributions the developer must raise before entering the Arts Building lease (also the cap on Arts Facility costs financed from public finance proceeds)
Public finance proceeds the Port commits to the arts program (Noonan replacement space, a community facility and the Arts Building)
Security instrument the developer provides for its Noonan tenant replacement-space and Arts Building obligations

facts.value: FC Pier 70, LLC, an affiliate of Brookfield Properties (originally Forest City)
Port of San Francisco (Seawall Lot 349; option parcels are ground-leased for 99 years except condominium parcels, which may be sold)
SITELAB urban studio (lead author); Grimshaw Architecture (commercial), David Baker Architects (residential), James Corner Field Operations (landscape)
Arts (the D4D permits office uses in E4 except on the ground floor; Priority Retail required on at least 33% of its east and south frontages, S2.2.3)
50 (D4D Figure 6.4.2), the lowest of any new parcel
90,000 sq ft arts facility with replacement studio space (Port project page); 'waterfront arts facility' in the 2018 groundbreaking release
50 years at $1/year base rent with a 15-year extension option, per the 2017 DDA major terms (the memo's mark-up also shows '66 year lease')
Excluded from the developer's option under the DDA, with the affordable parcels, C1A and historic Buildings 12 and 21
Phase 2C with E1 and Building 21 (Port's proposed 2026 phasing plan, Exhibit A)
Permanent replacement space for the Noonan Building artists 'will likely be located on the site of Parcel E4', at restricted rents tied to the Port's parameter rent (then $1.30/gsf)

open_questions: No arts operator, fundraising progress toward the $17.5 million, or design for the Arts Building was found; the DDA ties its start to three years after completion of the office building on Parcel 'B-2'.
SF YIMBY's 2021 summary attributes ~115,000 gsf of retail and arts space to Building 21 and ~120,000 gsf to 'E-1A and E-1B', with no separate arts building; the underlying filing was not retrieved.
Whether the Noonan Building has been demolished or its tenants relocated to temporary space: the June 2025 Port deck still lists 'Noonan Open Studios' and the Noonan Artists as active on site.
